source_text: Audi igitur, contra ea quae dixisti, breviter: non sunt Ecclesiae catholicae pectora, quae sermo tuus convenit, si a pietate et ratione discordant. Quod utrumque committunt, cum nec de Dei aequitate bene aestimant, nec mysteriorum, quae criminantur, sapientiam et divitias intellegunt. Non est haec fides antiquitus tradita atque fundata, nisi in conciliis malignantium, inspirata a diabolo, prolata a Manichaeo, celebrata a Marcione, Fausto, Adimanto, omnibusque eorum satellitibus, et nunc a te in Italiam, quod graviter gemimus, eructata.
pass_a_gloss: Hear therefore, against those things which you have said, briefly: they are not the breasts of the catholic Church which your speech convenes, if they discord from piety and from reason. Which both they commit, when they neither estimate well about the equity of God, nor understand the wisdom and riches of the mysteries which they charge. This is not the faith handed down from antiquity and founded, except in councils of those doing evil, inspired by the devil, brought forth by the Manichaean, celebrated by Marcion, Faustus, Adimantus, and all their satellites, and now belched by you into Italy, which we groan heavily.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Hear, then, a brief reply to what you said. The hearts your speech addresses are not those of the catholic Church if they are at odds with piety and reason. They offend against both when they neither think rightly about God's fairness nor understand the wisdom and riches of the mysteries they malign. This is no faith handed down and established from ancient times, except in councils of evildoers: inspired by the devil, proclaimed by Mani, celebrated by Marcion, Faustus, Adimantus, and all their followers, and now belched out by you into Italy, to our profound grief.

choices.why: Julian's divine-justice vocabulary; keep fairness rather than flattening into iustitia.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
